memoryTip: CAM + EL — one M, ends in EL
sampleUsage: A camel stores water in its hump.

memoryTip: CY + CLIST — CY says SY sound
sampleUsage: Every cyclist wore a safety helmet.

memoryTip: GYM + NAST — silent G makes J sound
sampleUsage: The gymnast did a perfect backflip.

memoryTip: COL + LECT — double L in collect
sampleUsage: She likes to collect colorful rocks.

memoryTip: GOS + SIP — double S in gossip
sampleUsage: Spreading gossip is unkind and hurtful.

memoryTip: SEN + ATE — ends in ATE like a plate
sampleUsage: The senate voted on the new law.

memoryTip: VER + Y — one R, ends in Y
sampleUsage: She was very happy about her grade.

memoryTip: VAR + Y — one R, AR vowel team
sampleUsage: Temperatures vary a lot in spring.

memoryTip: CRUISE — ends in ISE not IZE
sampleUsage: Our family went on a tropical cruise.

memoryTip: A + MONG — no U in among
sampleUsage: She was the tallest among her friends.

memoryTip: BAN + DIT — one T at the end
sampleUsage: The bandit hid behind the big rock.

memoryTip: COM + ET — one M, ends in ET
sampleUsage: A bright comet streaked across the sky.

memoryTip: COL + LEGE — double L in college
sampleUsage: My sister will start college next year.

memoryTip: WEAR — EA vowel team for clothing
sampleUsage: Wear your raincoat on rainy days.

memoryTip: CER + E + AL — three syllables, say slowly
sampleUsage: I eat cereal for breakfast every morning.

memoryTip: GIR + AFFE — double F and silent E
sampleUsage: A giraffe has a very long neck.

memoryTip: QUO + TIENT — the answer you get after dividing
sampleUsage: The quotient of ten divided by two is five.

memoryTip: RE + CI + PRO + CAL — flip the fraction
sampleUsage: The reciprocal of one half is two.

memoryTip: DE + NOMI + NATOR — the bottom number of a fraction
sampleUsage: The denominator tells how many parts in total.

memoryTip: NUMER + ATOR — the top number of a fraction
sampleUsage: The numerator shows how many parts you have.

memoryTip: SIMIL + AR — same shape, different size
sampleUsage: The two triangles are similar in shape.

memoryTip: ALL has double L at the end
sampleUsage: All the kids played outside.
He ate all his dinner.
The milk smells bad.
Put your books in the bag.

memoryTip: BAKE a cake — silent E at the end
sampleUsage: Let's bake some cookies.

memoryTip: BAND plays music — B + A + N + D
sampleUsage: The band played music at school.
He hit the ball with a bat.

memoryTip: BED — B + E + D, where you sleep

memoryTip: BEE has double E like two wings
